newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram postpones budget statement.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram postpones budget statement.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Tuesday postponed a statement on the proposed 1996/97 (April-March) budget because of a disruption in parliament over political developments in a western state.

A senior aide to the minister said the finance minister, who had been expected to discuss the proposed budget before the lower house of parliament on Tuesday afternoon, would possibly make the statement on Wednesday.
Instead of a full-fledged statement on the budget, Chidambaram made a brief announcement in the lower house of parliament, or Lok Sabha, relating to a proposed change in cotton fabric excise taxes.

The aide said the finance minister was now prepared to reply on Wednesday to parliamentary committees which have examined the proposed budget, but that the timing would depend on parliament's schedule,
The schedule of both houses of parliament was disrupted on Tuesday by noisy protests by the main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) over political developments in the western state of Gujarat.
BJP lawmakers objected to a decision by the deputy speaker of the Gujarat assembly to recognise a breakaway faction of BJP in the state.
Chidambaram was expected to make a second, more detailed reply to the budget proposals, outlining specific concessions to industrial sectors, next week, possibly on September 9 or 10, the aide said.

Financial markets expect Chidambaram to offer concessions to selected industries, including relief from a proposed minimum corporate tax, and possibly announce measures to attract small investors to stock markets.
Parliament is expected to vote on the budget plan by September 13, when the current session is scheduled to adjourn.
